## iBOT and Hybrid Objectives {#sec-ibot-hybrid}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Sources for this section"}

| # | Source | Summary |

| 2 | [DINOv2 (Oquab et al.)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.07193) | Combined DINO + iBOT + KoLeo; separate heads |

### The Gap Pure DINO Leaves {#sec-ibot-motivation}

DINO excels at global [CLS] features and emergent attention maps (@sec-dino-v1). Dense tasks (segmentation, depth, patch retrieval) benefit from **patch-level** alignment, not just [CLS] agreement across crops. iBOT ("image BERT pre-training with Online Tokenizer") fills that gap by applying self-distillation to masked patch tokens ([Zhou et al., 2022](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.07832)).

Maya needs vessel boundaries at patch resolution for a frozen-backbone segmenter. Pure DINO gives promising attention maps; iBOT and DINOv2 train patch tokens explicitly for that use case.

### iBOT Framework {#sec-ibot-framework}

iBOT recasts masked image modeling as knowledge distillation. BEiT distills from a **fixed** discrete tokenizer (dVAE). iBOT uses the **momentum teacher** as an online tokenizer: the teacher sees the full image; the student sees a masked version and must match teacher patch outputs on masked positions ([Zhou et al., 2022](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.07832)).

Two losses run in parallel:

**[CLS] loss (DINO-style):** cross-view self-distillation on class tokens.

$$
\mathcal{L}_{\texttt{[CLS]}} = -P_{\theta'}^{\texttt{[CLS]}}(\mathbf{v})^{\top} \log P_{\theta}^{\texttt{[CLS]}}(\mathbf{u})
$$ {#eq-ibot-cls}

**MIM patch loss:** masked patch distillation within the same view.

$$
\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{MIM}} = -\sum_{i=1}^{N} m_i \cdot P_{\theta'}^{\mathrm{patch}}(u_i)^{\top} \log P_{\theta}^{\mathrm{patch}}(\hat{u}_i)
$$ {#eq-ibot-mim}

Here $m_i$ is the mask indicator, $\hat{u}$ the masked student input, and teacher patch outputs come from the unmasked view. The teacher tokenizer is jointly learned via EMA; no offline dVAE stage.

iBOT shares projection heads between [CLS] and patches in the original paper (unlike DINOv2 at scale). Mask ratio $r$ is random: 0 with probability 0.5, else uniform in [0.1, 0.5] ([Zhou et al., 2022](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.07832)). ImageNet-1K ViT-B/16 reaches 79.5% linear probing and 77.1% k-NN; ViT-L/16 on ImageNet-22K reaches 82.3% linear and 87.8% fine-tune.

### DINOv2's Combined Loss {#sec-dinov2-combined-loss}

DINOv2 explicitly combines three terms ([Oquab et al., 2023](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.07193)):

**DINO (image-level):**

$$
\mathcal{L}_{\text{DINO}} = -\sum p_t \log p_s
$$ {#eq-dinov2-dino}

Cross-entropy between centered/sharpened teacher prototype scores $p_t$ and student scores $p_s$ on [CLS] tokens from different crops.

**iBOT (patch-level):**

$$
\mathcal{L}_{\text{iBOT}} = -\sum_i p_{ti} \log p_{si}
$$ {#eq-dinov2-ibot}

Summed over masked patch indices $i$, with separate iBOT MLP heads on patch tokens.

**KoLeo (spread regularizer):**

$$
\mathcal{L}_{\text{koleo}} = -\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\log(d_{n,i}), \quad d_{n,i} = \min_{j \neq i}\|x_i - x_j\|
$$ {#eq-koleo}

Applied to $\ell_2$-normalized [CLS] features in a batch; encourages uniform spacing on the hypersphere ([Sablayrolles et al., 2019](https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.13290), cited in DINOv2).

DINOv2 uses **separate MLP heads** for DINO and iBOT. iBOT originally shared heads; at scale DINOv2 found sharing hurts ([Oquab et al., 2023](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.07193)). Teacher weights still come from EMA; Sinkhorn-Knopp centering can replace softmax centering ([Caron et al., 2020](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.09882)).

```{.d2}
direction: right

classes: {
  input: { style.fill: "#EFF6FF"; style.stroke: "#3B82F6" }
  process: { style.fill: "#F0FDF4"; style.stroke: "#22C55E" }
  output: { style.fill: "#FFF7ED"; style.stroke: "#F97316" }
}

Image: Input image\ncrops {class: input}
Student: Student ViT\n(CLS + patches) {class: process}
Teacher: Teacher ViT\n(EMA) {class: process}

DHead: DINO head\n-> L_DINO {class: output}
IHead: iBOT head\n-> L_iBOT {class: output}
Koleo: "KoLeo on\n[CLS] batch" {class: output}

Image -> Student
Image -> Teacher
Student -> DHead
Student -> IHead
Student -> Koleo
Teacher -> DHead
Teacher -> IHead
```

### Why the Hybrid Wins {#sec-hybrid-why}

Global DINO loss clusters images semantically across augmentations. Patch iBOT loss aligns local token semantics for dense downstream tasks. KoLeo prevents representational collapse in [CLS] space and helps k-NN. Neither alone covers both global classification probes and pixel-level feature quality at foundation-model scale.

::: {.callout-note title="Think Hard: Why does DINOv2 untie heads when iBOT tied them?"}
At small scale, shared heads transfer [CLS] semantics to patch tokens beneficially ([Zhou et al., 2022](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.07832)). At ViT-g scale and 142M images, competing gradient signals on one MLP destabilize or dilute patch-specific learning. Separate heads let DINO optimize global invariance and iBOT optimize masked patch matching without capacity interference ([Oquab et al., 2023](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.07193)).
:::

### Maya Uses Pretrained DINOv2 {#sec-maya-ibot}

Maya does not train iBOT from scratch. She downloads DINOv2 ViT-L/14 weights (trained with the combined loss on LVD-142M) and extracts patch features for a lightweight segmentation head. The iBOT term in DINOv2 pretraining is why patch-level cosine similarity maps look semantically coherent (PCA of patch features in DINOv2 Figure 1). @sec-dinov2 covers data curation and scaling that make these weights possible.

### Worked Example: Patch Loss on a Single Masked Token {#sec-ibot-worked-example}

Consider one patch index $i$ masked in the student view. The teacher outputs $K$-dimensional logits on the corresponding visible patch, centered and sharpened into $p_{ti}$. The student head outputs $p_{si}$ on the mask token position. The iBOT contribution is a single cross-entropy $-\sum_k p_{ti}^{(k)} \log p_{si}^{(k)}$. Summing over all masked indices gives $\mathcal{L}_{\text{iBOT}}$.

If the teacher assigns high probability to prototype dimension $k=42$ for a vessel patch, the student must raise $p_{si}^{(42)}$ even though the student input hid that patch. The teacher never sees the mask; it supplies semantic targets. This is why iBOT targets are "semantic-level" compared to MAE pixels: prototypes encode cluster structure learned jointly with the backbone.

DINOv2 applies the same formula at scale with **blockwise masking** on student global crops, separate iBOT MLP heads, and Sinkhorn-Knopp centering on the teacher ([Oquab et al., 2023](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.07193)). KoLeo runs on the batch of [CLS] embeddings before the DINO head, encouraging no two retinal images in a minibatch to collapse to identical global vectors.

### iBOT vs BEiT vs MAE Targets {#sec-ibot-target-comparison}

| Method | Target | Tokenizer | Stages |
|--------|--------|-----------|--------|
| MAE | Normalized pixels | None | One |
| BEiT | Discrete dVAE codes | Offline dVAE | Two |
| BEiT v2 | VQ-KD codes | Offline VQ-KD | Two |
| iBOT | Softmax prototype distribution | Online EMA teacher | One |
| DINOv2 iBOT | Same as iBOT | EMA + SK centering | One |

Maya's choice: if she must train from scratch on fundus data only, iBOT-style joint training is simpler than training a BEiT tokenizer first. If she uses public weights, DINOv2 already paid that cost on LVD-142M.

### Training Dynamics at Scale {#sec-ibot-scale-notes}

The Lightly AI blog summarizes DINOv2 for engineers: three loss branches, separate heads, longer training, high-res finisher ([Lightly, 2023](https://www.lightly.ai/blog/dinov2)). Memory tricks (sequence packing, FlashAttention) exist because simultaneously forwarding global 224² crops, local 98² crops, masked patch paths, and dual heads multiplies activation cost. Maya training iBOT locally on 10k images should start with DINO-only pretrain before adding patch masking; ablations in iBOT show both branches contribute, but DINO alone is the simpler baseline (@sec-dino-v1).
